commits.subject: Torrents: the DHT joins through four public routers, and the port picked is kept (#650) (#664)
changelog: - Torrents: magnet links without trackers find peers through the DHT again where its first nodes didn't answer. MDM asked only two public routers to join the DHT; where neither answered (one name pointing at an old address, or a network blocking one), the DHT stayed empty and the log said "error in bootstrap" every minute or two. It now asks four together (`dht.libtorrent.org`, `dht.transmissionbt.com`, `router.bittorrent.com`, `router.utorrent.com`), any one that answers is enough, and the others are asked no more once one has. The nodes it knows are kept for the next start, the IPv6 ones too ([#650](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/650)).

- Torrents: with the **Port** box empty in Torrent settings, MDM keeps the port it picked and listens on it again at the next start (another one if a program has taken it), so peers that learned it, and a router's or firewall's rule for it, still reach MDM; it was a new port at each start. MDM's log says where it listens: one socket for IPv4 and IPv6, which Windows' `netstat -p tcp` (IPv4 only) doesn't list ([#650](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/650)).

commits.subject: Downloads to a slow disk: no freezes past the first gigabytes, no healthy connection cut as slow (#782) (#791)
changelog: - Fast downloads to a hard disk no longer freeze for 7 to 10 seconds once they are a few gigabytes in, and MDM no longer replaces healthy connections as "much slower than the other connections". Past the first gigabytes the system's cache is full and the disk sets the pace; each save of the resume state then had more to write than the last (spaced out by how long the last one took), until one took over 10 seconds and the download stood still. And a connection that had waited for the disk read what the system kept for it meanwhile in a burst, which MDM took for its speed, so every other connection looked four times slower and was cut, often all at once. Now the connections keep receiving into memory while the disk takes their writes (up to 256 MB per download), the resume state is saved to the disk only when that won't stop them, a connection's speed counts all the time it took (waits for the disk included), and no connection is replaced while the disk sets the pace. On a disk slower than the network the download goes at the disk's speed, evenly: with a test disk of 70 MB/s behind a 1 GB cache, a 6 GB download that froze for 7 to 12 seconds now never drops under 69 MB/s once the cache is full, and on Linux with the disk held to 60 MB/s, where MDM cut 67 connections in a typical 6 GB download (up to 111), it now cuts none or one. What a crash or power cut makes MDM download again is what came since the last save: on a disk that falls behind, everything since it did; pausing and stopping still save everything ([#782](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/782)).

It mirrors in right-to-left languages, shows a ring around it for the keyboard, shrinks to its logo, arrow and ✕ on a small video or where its words wouldn't fit, and shows the edge and the spots it snaps to while you drag it ([#703](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/703)).
